subject: Security exhibit: pen-test window, attack surface & evidence cadence
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@atlashealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pen-test window & attack-surface mapping

Hi Markus / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Before Legal and Security sign off on the order form we need to confirm a couple items in the security exhibit so our internal InfoSec team can schedule the assessment: 

1) Attack surface definition — we need a concrete list of endpoints, admin consoles, and any customer-facing integrations that will be in scope.
2) Pen-test window — preferred 72-hour windows vs. rolling 30-day window? We need to lock dates to avoid overlap with our maintenance windows.
3) Evidence rhythm — what artifacts will Redwood provide (SOC 2 report, AV logs, pen-test summary) and cadence (one-off vs. weekly snapshots during the test).

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our initial questions (initial_questions.xlsx) and a sample internal checklist. Can you propose a target schedule and the minimal evidence set required for a successful review?

Also copying our security alias in case they want to chime in: security@atlashealth.com

Thanks,

Jane Doe
Security Programs Manager
AtlasHealth
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pen-test window & attack-surface mapping

Jane — thanks for the clear list. Quick proposal to keep things narrow and non-disruptive: 

- Attack surface (proposed): public API endpoints (api.redwood.com/*), customer console (console.redwood.com), OAuth callback endpoints used by AtlasHealth, and the dedicated sandbox environment for Atlas (vpc-atlas-01). We will exclude internal monitoring endpoints and our internal CI/CD systems unless you specifically request them.

- Pen-test window (proposed): a two-week testing window with testing activity limited to weekday business hours for the first 72 hours, with the remainder used for low-impact validation. Alternatively we can run a rolling 30-day window if you need more flexibility. We recommend providing 7 business days' notice before the start date so our on-call ops can be scheduled.

- Evidence rhythm (proposed): 
  * Pre-test: SOC 2 Type II latest report (redacted where required), network diagram, list of in-scope IPs.
  * During test: daily summary emails and one consolidated log export at the end of each test week.
  * Post-test: executive summary + full remediation tracker and raw pen-test report (sensitive findings redacted on the public copy).

I've attached our suggested redlines to the security exhibit (redlines_ATLAS_v2.docx) and a draft pen-test schedule (pen-test-schedule.csv) to show the two-week option. 

Legal / pricing note: Karthik, can you confirm whether these proposed limits create any conflict with the order form language around audit rights? If not, we'll ask Atlas to accept the redlined exhibit and then routing to Legal to finalize.

Thanks,

— Markus Klein
Senior Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: redlines_ATLAS_v2.docx, pen-test-schedule.csv
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@atlashealth.com>

Cc: security@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pen-test window & attack-surface mapping

Markus — this is helpful. A couple of notes from InfoSec after an internal sync: 

- Attack surface: confirm the OAuth callback endpoints are included — our integration team needs to validate token exchange behavior. If you can provide a short list of exact URIs we can sign off quickly.

- Pen-test window: we insist on at least 48 hours notice for any high-impact tests (load or exploitative checks). The two-week window with business-hours-first model is acceptable provided that Redwood confirms a non-disruptive approach and has rollback runbooks.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is required. Additionally we request the latest pen-test raw findings under an NDA; redacted executive report is fine for public docs but we need the full technical findings for our remediation planning.

I've attached a marked-up draft with inline comments (redlines_from_atlas.docx). Our procurement counsel also asked to see the proposed audit-rights clause in the MSA; if possible please surface the specific paragraph number so their legal team can mirror edits.

On the timing: we can target the week of Aug 2 as a tentative window if Redwood can commit to the 7 business days' notice prior to starting the active tests.

Thanks — Jane
